question:
**Case Study 1: Fuel Consumption and Speed**

The relation between fuel consumption $F(l/100km)$ and speed $V(km/h)$ is given as:

$F=\frac{V^{2}}{500}-\frac{V}{4}+14$

(i) Find F when V = 40 km/h.

(ii) Find $\frac{dF}{dV}$.

(iii) (a) Find the speed V for which fuel consumption F is minimum.

OR

(iii) (b) Find the quantity of fuel required to travel 600 km at the speed V at which $\frac{dF}{dV}=-0.01$.
explanation:
(i) $F=7.2$ l/100km.

(ii) $\frac{dF}{dV}=\frac{V}{250}-\frac{1}{4}$.

(iii)(a) Minimum when $V=62.5$ km/h.

OR

(iii)(b) For $V=60$ km/h fuel required for 600 km = $37.2$ litres.

options.A:
(i) $F=7.2$ l/100km.
(ii) $\frac{dF}{dV}=\frac{V}{250}-\frac{1}{4}$.
(iii)(a) Minimum when $V=62.5$ km/h.
OR
(iii)(b) For $V=60$ km/h, fuel required for 600 km is $37.2$ litres.
options.B:
(i) $F=8.2$ l/100km.
(ii) $\frac{dF}{dV}=\frac{V}{500}-\frac{1}{4}$.
(iii)(a) Minimum when $V=125$ km/h.
OR
(iii)(b) For $V=60$ km/h, fuel required for 600 km is $49.2$ litres.
options.C:
(i) $F=7.2$ l/100km.
(ii) $\frac{dF}{dV}=\frac{V}{250}+\frac{1}{4}$.
(iii)(a) Minimum when $V=50$ km/h.
OR
(iii)(b) For $V=40$ km/h, fuel required for 600 km is $43.2$ litres.
options.D:
(i) $F=6.2$ l/100km.
(ii) $\frac{dF}{dV}=\frac{V}{250}-\frac{1}{4}$.
(iii)(a) Minimum when $V=60$ km/h.
OR
(iii)(b) For $V=62.5$ km/h, fuel required for 600 km is $37.2$ litres.
